rules.title: Security deposit cap of one month's rent (two months for qualifying small landlords)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security, however denominated, above one month's rent in addition to first month's rent. A small landlord (a natural person or an LLC of natural persons owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units total) may collect up to two months' rent, except from a service member.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords; 1 month for service members)
rules.coverage_conditions: Security for rental agreements for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling; applies to security collected or demanded on or after July 1, 2024.
rules.exemptions: Small landlords (natural person or LLC whose members are all natural persons, owning no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four units total) may collect up to two months' rent, but not from service members. Advance payment of not less than six months' rent is allowed for leases of six months or longer. Agreed fees for tenant-requested alterations are allowed.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Higher two-month cap depends on landlord being a natural person/LLC of natural persons and on total portfolio (≤2 properties, ≤4 units); not available if tenant is a service member.

rules.penalty: Bad faith claim or retention of security may subject the landlord to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages.
rules.quoted_span: (c) (1) Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date inferred from subdivision (c)(6), which exempts security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024.

rules.title: Service member higher-deposit disclosure and return
rules.requirement: If a landlord charges a service member a higher than standard security due to credit or housing history, it must give a written statement explaining why by lease signing, and must return the additional amount after no more than six months if the tenant is not in arrears.
rules.coverage_conditions: Service members (as defined in Mil. & Vet. Code § 400) renting residential property in which they will reside, charged higher than standard security.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only when the tenant is a service member and is charged a higher than standard security.

rules.title: Return of deposit with itemized statement within 21 days
rules.requirement: Within 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates, the landlord must furnish an itemized statement of deductions with supporting documents and return the remaining security. A landlord who in bad faith fails to comply forfeits any claim to the security.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential tenancies where security is held.
rules.exemptions: Receipts/documentation not required if deductions for repairs and cleaning total $125 or less or tenant validly waived, unless tenant requests documentation within 14 days.
rules.penalty: Statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security for bad faith retention, plus actual damages; forfeiture of claim to security for bad faith noncompliance.
rules.quoted_span: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises, but not earlier than the time that either the landlord or the tenant provides a notice to terminate the tenancy under Section 1946 or 1946.1, Section 1161 of the Code of Civil Procedure, or not earlier than 60 calendar days prior to
rules.conflict_note: Document does not state the original effective date of the 21-day rule; section as currently amended effective January 1, 2026.

rules.title: Electronic return of deposit when rent/security paid electronically
rules.requirement: If the landlord received the security or rent electronically, it must return the remaining security electronically to an account designated by the tenant (unless otherwise agreed in writing) and must notify the tenant of this right before the tenancy ends.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies where the landlord received the security or rental payments electronically.
rules.exemptions: Not applicable where parties agreed in writing to another return method, or tenancy terminated under CCP § 1161(2)-(4) (notice requirement).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where security or rent was paid electronically.

rules.title: Move-in and move-out photograph requirement
rules.requirement: Landlords must photograph the unit at move-out before and after repairs or cleanings that will be deducted (from April 1, 2025) and at move-in for tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025. Photos must accompany deductions.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies with security deposits; move-in photos for tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025.
rules.quoted_span: (2) Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned to the landlord, but prior to any repairs or cleanings for which the landlord will make a deduction from or claim against the security deposit pursuant to this section, and shall also take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after such repairs or cleanings are completed.
rules.conflict_note: Move-in photo requirement begins for tenancies starting on or after July 1, 2025.

rules.title: Tenant right to pre-move-out initial inspection
rules.requirement: The landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the right to request an initial inspection before move-out, and upon request inspect and give an itemized list of proposed deductions so the tenant can cure them.
rules.exemptions: Not applicable when tenancy terminated under CCP § 1161(2), (3), or (4).
rules.quoted_span: (f) (1) Within a reasonable time after notification of either party’s intention to terminate the tenancy, or before the end of the lease term, the landlord shall notify the tenant in writing of the tenant’s option to request an initial inspection and of the tenant’s right to be present at the inspection.

rules.title: Deductions limited; no charges for ordinary wear and tear or preexisting conditions
rules.requirement: Landlords may deduct only amounts reasonably necessary for unpaid rent, damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, cleaning to move-in condition, and restoring property, and may not charge for preexisting damage, ordinary wear and tear, or unnecessary professional cleaning.
rules.penalty: Statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security for bad faith claims, plus actual damages.
rules.quoted_span: (2) (A) The landlord shall not assert a claim against the tenant or the security for damages to the premises or any defective conditions that preexisted the tenancy, for ordinary wear and tear or the effects thereof, whether the wear and tear preexisted the tenancy or occurred during the tenancy, or for the cumulative effects of ordinary wear and tear occurring during any one or more tenancies.

rules.title: Ban on nonrefundable security
rules.requirement: A lease or rental agreement may not characterize any security as nonrefundable.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential leases and rental agreements.
rules.quoted_span: (n) A lease or rental agreement shall not contain a provision characterizing any security as “nonrefundable.”

rules.title: Statutory damages for bad faith retention of security
rules.requirement: Bad faith claim or retention of security, or a bad faith demand for replacement security, may subject the landlord or successor to statutory damages of up to twice the security plus actual damages; the landlord bears the burden of proving reasonableness.
rules.key_value: Up to 2x the security plus actual damages
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential tenancies with security deposits.
rules.penalty: Statutory damages up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages.
rules.quoted_span: (m) The bad faith claim or retention by a landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest of the security or any portion thereof in violation of this section, or the bad faith demand of replacement of security in violation of subdivision (k), may subject the landlord or the landlord’s successors in interest to statutory damages of up to twice the amount of the security, in addition to actual damages.
